extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners, patent applicants and practitioners (agents/attorneys) dealing with priority claims under the Paris Convention / PCT (Republic of Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for formal and substantive examination of patent applications claiming priority (international/Treaty and domestic priority) under the Korean Patent Act, including timing, evidential-document rules, identicalness/retroactivity standards, and special treatment for US CIPs/provisionals and multiple priority claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid priority claims based on hypothetical/unspecified/other-entity applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant filed an application claiming a priority under the Treaty based on a hypothetical application, an application filed by another entity or an application which cannot be specified, the applicant shall not be able to amend or add a priority claim since the priority claim is basically invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority claims must be based on concrete, identifiable prior applications; speculative or unspecified bases cannot be remedied by amendment or addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No amendment/addition of priority claim after withdrawal/invalidity or final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a priority claim under the Treaty has been withdrawn or invalidated, or where an application claiming priority has been invalidated, withdrawn or abandoned, or where a decision to grant/reject an application becomes final and conclusive, the applicant shall not be able to amend or add the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time when a decision to grant becomes final is when a certified copy of the decision to grant is served; for a rejection it is when 30 days have elapsed after service of a certified copy of the rejection. Addition of a priority claim made on the same date as withdrawal of all priority claims may be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments (withdrawal/part-withdrawal/correction/adding) allowed within one year and four months
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one year and four months from the earliest filing date, withdrawal of all priority claims, withdrawal of part of multiple priority claims, correction of clerical errors in priority claims, and addition of priority claims shall be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When withdrawing and adding priority claims within this period, the applicant need not submit a separate withdrawal document and may submit a single amendment reflecting both withdrawal and addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: After one year and four months only clerical corrections permitted (no additions/changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments of a priority claim after one year and four months has elapsed shall be permitted only when correcting clerical errors in the indication of the priority claim; changing/specifying/adding the first application is not allowed. However, withdrawal of all or part of priority claims in multiple claims remains allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory period is strict: additions or specification of the first application after 1 year 4 months are not allowed; examiner may allow only clerical amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine formalities of a priority claim first; invalidate proceedings if not corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an application claiming priority under the Treaty or an amendment is submitted, the examiner shall examine the formalities of the priority claim; if a deficiency is found, the examiner shall request amendment. If the applicant does not address the deficiency within the designated period the examiner can invalidate the proceedings for the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If priority proceedings are invalidated, the application is treated as a normal application without the priority claim; examiner should list formal deficiencies and give opportunity to amend within the statutory periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination requirements for priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Formality requirements include: identicalness of the applicants, the earliest filing date of the first application filed in a Treaty country, regularity of the first application, compliance with the priority period, description of the purport of the priority claim, and submission of evidential documents proving the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If part of multiple priority claims contain deficiencies, request amendment only for deficient claims; if not addressed, invalidate only those deficient priority claims rather than all, where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Patent Net / WIPO to verify evidential documents; request translations if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidential documents certifying priority in an international application can be checked via evidential documents posted on Patent Net or via the WIPO PCT database; if not available, the examiner may request the applicant to submit translations of evidential documents certifying the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If documents cannot be confirmed through these channels, examiner should request amendment and consider invalidating the priority claim only after giving applicant opportunity to explain or submit documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination: grant retroactive filing date per-invention if identical
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention described in the application claiming priority is identical to the one in the first application (as shown by specification/drawings), the examiner shall examine patentability based on the retroactive filing date of the first application; if not identical, examine based on the filing date of the application claiming priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rejecting without granting a retroactive filing date, the examiner must describe why retroactivity was not granted along with the grounds for rejection. Examiner may request translations of evidential documents when prior art search shows intervening prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identicalness standard: claims need match the disclosure of first application (not necessarily identical claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identicalness does not require the claims of both applications to be identical; rather the invention described in the claims of the later application must be identical to the invention described in the specification or drawings of the first application (apply Article 29(3) standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions are deemed identical in specific situations: (i) later app filed for part of the first app, (ii) later apps based on divisionals of the first app, (iii) single later app filed based on more than two first applications. Priority can be recognized by invention (i.e., per-invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of multiple priority claims (multiple first applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications with multiple priority claims, the examiner should not automatically reject for being based on two or more first applications; if inventions are not identical, examiner can cite violation (Article 45). Applicant may divide the application and retain priority for each divided application. Examiner examines based on earliest filing date of each invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claimed invention combines subject matter separately described only in different first applications (e.g., combining 'a' from A and 'b' from B), the invention is examined based on the actual filing date of the later (Korean) application (no retroactivity). If the earliest-filed priority among multiple is withdrawn, the examiner must determine whether the newly earliest-filed application can serve as the priority basis per Paris Convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-art search and choice of filing date for patentability examination
rubrics_metrics.description: If prior art (Article 29 or Article 36 prior-filed application) is not found between the filing date of the first application and the filing date of the priority-claiming application, examine patentability based on the filing date of the first application; if prior art exists, compare to determine whether the later invention is described in the first application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may request translations of evidential documents and compare documents to determine whether to apply retroactive filing date per invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for US-based priority claims: continuation-in-part (CIP) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority is based only on a US CIP and only the CIP specification was submitted as evidential documents, the examiner shall examine inventions based on the filing date without granting retroactivity; if the original application specification/drawings are submitted, follow other CIP guidelines. If an invention is only described in the CIP, the patentability date is the CIP filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subject matter is described in both original and CIP and the Treaty-filed application is within one year of the original, subject matter described in both takes the original's filing date; subject matter only in CIP takes CIP's filing date. If the Treaty-filed application is filed after one year from the original, retroactivity for the original may not be available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for US-based priority claims: provisional vs non-provisional
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a provisional application serves as the basis for priority depends on the USPTO's issuance of evidential documents certifying priority (e.g., priority documents, certified copy of original application). If no non-provisional is filed after the provisional, the provisional serves as the basis; if a non-provisional is filed claiming benefit, the provisional may be the basic application for priority and the priority period starts from the provisional filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine which US application the USPTO treated as the basis for priority by checking issued evidential documents; differences in the type of provisional affect which application is the basic application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to submit evidential documents within one year and four months causes loss of priority effect
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidential documents certifying priority are not submitted within one year and four months from the earliest filing date, the priority claim shall lose its effect. Evidential documents means more than the specification/drawings alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall request amendment and invalidate the priority claim procedure if documents are not submitted within the statutory period; procedural error cannot be cured after the period. For international patent applications, however, KIPO may allow submission of evidential documents after entering the national stage and accept them if submitted in response to the amendment request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic exchange / streamlined submission checks and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority is based on a first application filed in a country with a streamlined electronic exchange procedure and an application number is provided, examiner shall check whether evidential documents were exchanged electronically (except JPO and EPO). If exchange records cannot be checked within the submission period, examiner shall request amendment and invalidate the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In principle, evidential documents exchanged or submitted after the designated period cause the priority to lose effect (Article 54(6)), but if the applicant has completed legitimate exchange procedures in both countries the examiner may treat late-submitted/exchanged documents as legitimate and recognize the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory period for amendment/addition of priority claims is not extendable
rubrics_metrics.description: Period allowed for amendment or addition of a priority claim (Article 54(7)) is statutory and cannot be extended after one year and four months from the earliest filing date. Even if an amendment request was made within the period, once the one year and four months has elapsed, additions cannot be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one year and four months has elapsed (even if examiner had previously extended an amendment period), examiner may describe the refusal to accept amendments/additions with statutory basis in the written request for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority claim eligibility and exclusions (Article 55)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person may claim domestic priority based on an earlier-filed patent or utility model application on which they are entitled, except where: (1) the relevant application is filed more than one year after the prior-filed application; (2) the prior-filed application is a divisional/converted application as prescribed; (3) the prior-filed application has been abandoned, invalidated, or withdrawn; (4) a final/conclusive decision on grant/rejection/utility registration has been made before the relevant application is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must state intention and indicate the prior-filed application in the patent application. If requirements met, the later application may be deemed filed at the time of the prior-filed application for purposes of Articles 29, 30, 36, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority retroactivity and publication/laid-open effects
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying the main bodies of certain Articles (e.g., Article 29(3),(4)), the application claiming domestic priority which is identical to the invention in the prior-filed application shall be deemed to have been filed on the prior-filed application's filing date; if such an application is laid open or registered, the invention in the later application is deemed laid open for the prior-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraphs (3) and (4) do not apply where the prior-filed application itself contains a priority claim (including Article 4-D(1) Paris Convention priority claims). Also certain exceptions (e.g., voluntarily withdrawn international applications) are specified where Article 29(7) does not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 56 withdrawal rules and timing (domestic priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior-filed application to which priority is claimed shall be deemed withdrawn at the time one year and three months have elapsed from its filing date, except where it was already abandoned/invalidated/withdrawn, a final decision exists, or the priority claim itself has been withdrawn. No applicant shall withdraw the priority claim upon expiration of one year and three months from the filing date of the prior-filed application. If the later application is withdrawn within one year and three months, the priority claim shall be deemed withdrawn simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of the one year + three months (15 months) deemed-withdrawn timing; this affects the status of domestic priority claims and whether they can be maintained or withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purport/policy of domestic priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic priority claim allows protection for inventions developed from a prior-filed application to further specify, improve, or add to the prior-filed application; inventions identical to the prior-filed application are deemed filed on the prior filing date while newly added improvements are deemed filed on the later filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provision prevents irrational rejection of improvements as 'same invention' or improper addition of new matter—supports protection of follow-on refinements while preserving correct filing-date treatment per subject matter.
